p.src: When Lu Su had finished reading, he asked, “What is my lord’s esteemed opinion?” Sun Quan replied, “No conclusion has yet been reached.” Zhang Zhao said, “Cao Cao commands a million men and, invoking the Son of Heaven’s name, campaigns throughout the realm. To oppose him would be disobedience. Moreover, the great advantage by which my lord could resist Cao Cao was the Yangtze River. Now that Cao Cao has gained Jingzhou, he shares with us the strategic defenses of the Yangtze, and his power cannot be withstood. In my humble opinion, surrender is the surest course for complete safety.” All the other advisers said, “Zibu’s words accord perfectly with Heaven’s will.” Sun Quan pondered in silence. Zhang Zhao continued, “My lord need not harbor so many doubts. If you submit to Cao Cao, the people of Eastern Wu will enjoy peace, and the six commanderies south of the Yangtze will be preserved.” Sun Quan lowered his head and said nothing.

p.src: After a while, Sun Quan rose to change his clothes, and Lu Su followed behind him. Knowing what Lu Su intended, Sun Quan took his hand and asked, “What do you think should be done?” Lu Su replied, “What the others said just now gravely misleads you, General. All the others may surrender to Cao Cao; you alone, General, cannot surrender to him.” Sun Quan asked, “Why do you say so?” Lu Su replied, “If men such as I surrender to Cao Cao, I will be sent back among my fellow provincials and, after successive promotions, may still attain the office of governor or commandery administrator. But if you surrender to Cao Cao, General, where could you go? Your rank would rise no higher than marquis; you would have no more than one carriage, one mount, and a few attendants. How could you ever face south and style yourself lord? The others speak only for their own interests; you must not heed them. You should decide upon your great policy without delay.”

p.src: Sun Quan sighed and said, “The others’ arguments have sorely disappointed me. Zijing, the great policy you have expounded accords exactly with my own view. Heaven itself has bestowed you upon me! But Cao Cao has newly acquired Yuan Shao’s forces and, more recently, the troops of Jingzhou as well. I fear his power is too great to resist.” Lu Su said, “When I went to Jiangxia, I brought back Zhuge Liang, the younger brother of Zhuge Jin. He is here now. My lord may question him and thus learn the true situation.” Sun Quan asked, “Is Master Sleeping Dragon here?” Lu Su replied, “He is now resting at the posthouse.” Sun Quan said, “It is late today, so I shall not meet him yet. Tomorrow I shall assemble my civil and military officers beneath my command. Let him first behold the finest men of Jiangdong, and then we shall ascend the hall to deliberate affairs.”

p.src: Lu Su accepted the command and departed. The next day he went to the posthouse to see Kongming and again cautioned him, “When you meet my lord today, you must on no account speak of the size of Cao Cao’s army.” Kongming smiled and said, “I shall adapt to circumstances as I find them. There will certainly be no mistake.” Lu Su then led Kongming to the command tent. There they found Zhang Zhao, Gu Yong, and more than twenty other civil and military officers already waiting, in lofty caps and broad sashes, their garments arranged and themselves seated with solemn dignity. Kongming greeted them one by one and asked each man’s name. When the courtesies were complete, he took the guest’s seat. Zhang Zhao and the others, seeing Kongming’s graceful bearing and imposing presence, concluded that he must have come to persuade them. Zhang Zhao was the first to challenge him, saying, “I am but an insignificant scholar of Jiangdong. I have long heard that while you lived in seclusion at Longzhong, you compared yourself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi. Is that truly so?” Kongming replied, “That is but a modest comparison I have made throughout my life.” Zhang Zhao said, “I recently heard that Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, visited your thatched cottage three times and was fortunate enough to secure your service. He regarded it as a fish finding water and intended to sweep through Jingzhou and Xiangyang. Yet now, in a single stroke, all has fallen into Cao Cao’s hands. What strategy lay behind this?”

p.src: Kongming thought to himself that Zhang Zhao was the foremost adviser under Sun Quan, and that unless he first confounded this man, he could never persuade Sun Quan. He therefore replied, “In my view, taking the lands along the Han River would have been as easy as turning over my hand. But my lord, Liu of Yuzhou, personally practices benevolence and righteousness. He could not bear to seize the inheritance of one of his own imperial clan and therefore firmly refused it. Liu Cong was a mere child who trusted slanderous counsel and secretly surrendered, thereby allowing Cao Cao to run rampant. My lord is now stationed with his forces at Jiangxia and has another excellent design in mind—one that ordinary men cannot fathom.”

p.src: Zhang Zhao said, “If that is so, then your words and deeds contradict one another. You compare yourself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi. Guan Zhong served as chief minister to Duke Huan, made him hegemon over the feudal lords, and brought the realm to order. Yue Yi supported the weakened state of Yan and captured more than seventy cities of Qi. These two were truly men of talent capable of saving the age. While you were in your thatched cottage, you merely took lofty delight in the wind and moon and sat erect with your arms about your knees. Now that you have entered Liu Yuzhou’s service, you ought to benefit the living, remove their afflictions, and destroy the rebels who trouble the realm. Before Liu Yuzhou obtained your service, he could still range freely across the realm and hold cities and territory. When he gained you, all looked up to him with expectation. Even children three feet tall said that a fierce tiger had gained wings, and that they would soon see the Han house restored and the Cao clan destroyed. The old ministers of the court and recluses in the mountains alike wiped their eyes and waited, believing that now was the time when the clouds veiling the high heavens would be swept away, the radiance of sun and moon looked up to once more, the people rescued from fire and flood, and the realm laid upon a peaceful couch. Yet why is it that, since you joined Yuzhou, the moment Cao Cao’s army appeared, you cast away armor and weapons and fled at the mere rumor of its approach? Above, you could not repay Liu Biao by bringing peace to his people; below, you could not assist his orphaned son in holding the territory. Instead, you abandoned Xinye, fled to Fancheng, suffered defeat at Dangyang, and ran to Xiakou, until you had nowhere left to shelter. Thus, after Yuzhou obtained your service, he has fared worse than before. Did Guan Zhong and Yue Yi truly behave in such a fashion? These are merely the blunt words of a foolish man; I hope you will not take offense!”

p.src: When Kongming had heard him out, he smiled and said, “The great roc soars ten thousand li; how could common birds comprehend its ambition? Suppose a man is stricken with a lingering illness: one must first give him thin gruel to drink and mild medicine to take. Once his organs are restored to harmony and his body gradually recovers, he may then be nourished with meat and treated with potent medicine. Thus the root of the illness is wholly removed, and the man’s life is preserved. But if, before his vital energies have settled, one immediately administers powerful drugs and rich foods, it will indeed be difficult to keep him safe. My lord, Liu of Yuzhou, formerly suffered defeat at Runan and took refuge with Liu Biao. His troops numbered fewer than a thousand, and his commanders were limited to Guan, Zhang, and Zhao Yun. This was precisely like the moment when an illness has reduced a man to utter weakness. Xinye was a small, remote county among the hills, with few inhabitants and scant provisions. Yuzhou merely borrowed it as a temporary refuge; could he truly have intended to sit there and defend it forever? Yet though his arms were incomplete, his walls insecure, his troops untrained, and his provisions insufficient even from day to day, he burned the encampment at Bowang and unleashed the waters of the White River, making the likes of Xiahou Dun and Cao Ren tremble with terror. In my humble judgment, even Guan Zhong and Yue Yi could scarcely have surpassed such generalship. As for Liu Cong’s surrender to Cao Cao, Yuzhou truly knew nothing of it beforehand. Moreover, he could not bear to seize the patrimony of one of his own clan amid the disorder. This was true benevolence and righteousness. After the defeat at Dangyang, Yuzhou saw hundreds of thousands of people who had rallied to his righteous cause following him with the old supported and the young carried. Unable to abandon them, he advanced only ten li a day, gave no thought to seizing Jiangling, and willingly shared defeat with them. This too was great benevolence and righteousness. When the few contend with the many, victory and defeat are but ordinary fortunes of war. Long ago, the High Emperor was repeatedly defeated by Xiang Yu, yet won success in a single battle at Gaixia. Was that not due to Han Xin’s excellent strategy? Han Xin had long served the High Emperor, yet he had by no means won victory upon victory. The great designs of a state and the security or peril of its altars demand a true master strategist. They are not the province of boastful disputants who deceive others with empty fame and, when seated in debate or standing in discourse, seem unequalled. Yet when circumstances demand an improvised response, they have not a single useful ability among a hundred. Such men truly become the laughingstock of the realm!” This speech left Zhang Zhao without a single word of reply.

p.src: Suddenly, a man among those seated raised his voice and asked, “Lord Cao has a million troops encamped and a thousand officers arrayed beneath him. He advances like a soaring dragon and watches like a crouching tiger, poised to swallow Jiangxia whole. What do you make of that?” Kongming looked at him and saw that it was Yu Fan. Kongming said, “Cao Cao has gathered Yuan Shao’s antlike swarm of troops and coerced Liu Biao’s rabble into his service. Though they number several million, they are nothing to fear.” Yu Fan sneered. “Your army was defeated at Dangyang and your stratagems exhausted at Xiakou. You have come humbly begging aid from others, yet still claim to feel no fear. This is truly grand talk intended to deceive!” Kongming said, “How could Liu of Yuzhou’s few thousand benevolent and righteous troops oppose a million brutal men? He withdrew to defend Xiakou in order to await the proper time. Now Jiangdong has elite troops, ample provisions, and the natural barrier of the Yangtze, yet you would still have your lord bend the knee and surrender to the traitor, heedless of the world’s scorn. Judged by this, Liu of Yuzhou is indeed one who does not fear the traitor Cao!” Yu Fan could not answer.

p.src: Another man among those seated asked, “Do you intend to emulate the tongues of Zhang Yi and Su Qin and come lobbying Eastern Wu?” Kongming looked at him and saw that it was Bu Zhi. Kongming said, “Bu Zishan regards Su Qin and Zhang Yi merely as debaters, not knowing that they were also heroes of their age. Su Qin bore the seals of chancellor of six states, while Zhang Yi twice served as chancellor of Qin. Both possessed strategies to uphold and rescue the states they served; they were not men who feared the strong, bullied the weak, and shrank from blades and swords. You gentlemen hear Cao Cao utter empty and deceitful words and at once grow frightened and plead for surrender. How dare you mock Su Qin and Zhang Yi?” Bu Zhi fell silent and said nothing.

p.src: Suddenly another man asked, “What manner of man do you consider Cao Cao to be?” Kongming looked at the man and saw that it was Xue Zong. Kongming replied, “Cao Cao is a traitor to the Han. Why need you even ask?” Xue Zong said, “Your words are mistaken. The succession of the Han has endured until now, but its allotted span is nearing its end. Lord Cao already possesses two-thirds of the realm, and all men give him their allegiance. Liu of Yuzhou fails to recognize Heaven’s timing and stubbornly seeks to contend with him. That is precisely like striking a rock with an egg—how could he avoid defeat?” Kongming cried sternly, “Xue Jingwen, how can you utter such words, acknowledging neither father nor sovereign? A man living between Heaven and Earth must take loyalty and filial devotion as the foundations of his conduct. Since you are a minister of Han, whenever you see one who behaves as no minister should, you ought to swear to join in destroying him. Such is a minister’s duty. Cao Cao’s ancestors enjoyed the emoluments of Han, yet he thinks not of repaying the dynasty and instead harbors the ambition to usurp and rebel. All beneath Heaven share this indignation. Yet you attribute his success to Heaven’s decree. You are truly a man without father or sovereign! You are not worth speaking with! Say no more!” Xue Zong’s face filled with shame, and he could make no reply.

p.src: Another man among those seated immediately asked, “Though Cao Cao holds the Son of Heaven hostage to command the feudal lords, he is still a descendant of Cao Shen, Chancellor of State. Though Liu of Yuzhou claims descent from Prince Jing of Zhongshan, there is no evidence by which it can be verified. Plainly he is no more than a mat-weaver and sandal-peddler. How could he be worthy to contend with Cao Cao?” Kongming looked at him and saw that it was Lu Ji. Kongming laughed. “Are you not young Master Lu, who hid oranges in his robe while seated before Yuan Shu? Please sit quietly and hear what I have to say. If Cao Cao is indeed a descendant of Chancellor Cao, then his family has served as ministers of Han for generations. Yet now he monopolizes power, acts wantonly, and insults his sovereign and father. Thus he not only denies his sovereign but also despises his ancestors. He is not only a rebellious minister of the House of Han but also an unfilial traitor to the Cao clan! Liu of Yuzhou is an august descendant of the imperial house. The present Emperor examined the genealogy and granted him rank. How can you say there is no evidence? Moreover, the High Ancestor began as a mere village constable, yet ultimately gained the whole realm. What shame, then, is there in weaving mats and selling sandals? Your understanding is that of a child; you are not worthy to converse with men of lofty wisdom!” Lu Ji was left speechless.

p.src: Suddenly, one of those seated said, “Everything Kongming has said is forced sophistry, none of it sound argument. There is no need to say more. But tell me, Kongming: which of the classics do you study?” Kongming looked at him and saw that it was Yan Jun. Kongming said, “Those who hunt out chapters and pluck phrases are the pedants of the age. How could they revive a state or accomplish great deeds? In antiquity there were Yi Yin, who tilled the fields of Shen, and Ziya, who fished by the Wei; then men such as Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, and men such as Deng Yu and Geng Yan. All possessed talent sufficient to uphold the world, yet I do not know which classics any of them studied throughout their lives. Could they too have imitated bookish scholars, fussing narrowly amid brush and inkstone, quibbling over black and yellow, and doing nothing but playing with words?” Yan Jun lowered his head in dejection and could not answer.

u.src: Suddenly, one of those seated said, “Everything Kongming has said is forced sophistry, none of it sound argument. There is no need to say more.
But tell me, Kongming: which of the classics do you study?”
Kongming looked at him and saw that it was Yan Jun.
Kongming said, “Those who hunt out chapters and pluck phrases are the pedants of the age. How could they revive a state or accomplish great deeds?

In antiquity there were Yi Yin, who tilled the fields of Shen, and Ziya, who fished by the Wei; then men such as Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, and men such as Deng Yu and Geng Yan. All possessed talent sufficient to uphold the world, yet I do not know which classics any of them studied throughout their lives.
Could they too have imitated bookish scholars, fussing narrowly amid brush and inkstone, quibbling over black and yellow, and doing nothing but playing with words?”
Yan Jun lowered his head in dejection and could not answer.

p.src: Suddenly another man cried out, “You delight in grandiose talk, but may possess no true learning. I fear you will merely be laughed at by scholars.” Kongming looked at the man and saw that it was Cheng Deshu of Runan. Kongming replied, “Among scholars there are gentlemen and petty men. The gentleman scholar is loyal to his sovereign and loves his country, upholds righteousness and detests evil, striving to extend his beneficence to his own age and leave his name to posterity. The petty scholar, however, devotes himself solely to trivial embellishments and specializes only in writing. In youth he composes ornate rhapsodies, and in white-haired age he exhausts himself over the classics. Though a thousand words may flow from his brush, not a single strategy resides in his breast. Take Yang Xiong: though famed throughout the age for his writings, he demeaned himself by serving Wang Mang and could not escape death after throwing himself from a tower. He was what may be called a petty scholar. Even if such a man composed ten thousand words a day, what value would there be in him?” Cheng Deshu could not answer.

p.src: When they saw Kongming answer with such ready fluency, they all turned pale. At that moment, Zhang Wen and Luo Tong, who were among those present, were about to challenge him again. Suddenly a man entered from outside and cried sternly, “Kongming is an extraordinary talent of our age. For you gentlemen to assail him with mere verbal disputation is no proper way to honor a guest. Cao Cao’s great army is at our borders, yet instead of devising a plan to repel the enemy, are you merely going to wage a war of words?” They looked at the man and saw that he was Huang Gai, styled Gongfu, a native of Lingling and presently an officer in charge of provisions in Eastern Wu. Huang Gai then said to Kongming, “I have heard that profiting from many words is not so good as remaining silent. Why not present your weighty counsel to our lord instead of debating with all these men?” Kongming replied, “These gentlemen understand nothing of the affairs of the age and questioned me one after another, so I could hardly refrain from answering.”

p.src: Thereupon Huang Gai and Lu Su conducted Kongming inside. At the middle gate they happened to meet Zhuge Jin, and Kongming saluted him. Zhuge Jin said, “Worthy brother, since you have come to the Southland, why did you not visit me?” Kongming replied, “Since I serve Governor Liu, reason demands that I put public duty before private concerns. My official business is not yet concluded, so I have not dared attend to family matters. I trust you will forgive me.” Zhuge Jin said, “After you have met the Marquis of Wu, come and talk with me.” With that, he went his way.

p.src: Lu Su said, “Do not forget what I asked of you just now.” Kongming nodded and assented. When Kongming was conducted into the hall, Sun Quan descended the steps to welcome him and received him with exceptional courtesy. After they had exchanged salutations, Kongming was offered a seat. The civil and military officers stood in two ranks. Lu Su stood beside Kongming, intent only on hearing what he would say. After conveying Xuande’s intentions, Kongming stole a glance at Sun Quan: blue-eyed, purple-bearded, and imposing in appearance. Kongming thought to himself, “This man has an uncommon countenance. He can only be provoked, not persuaded. When he questions me, I shall simply provoke him with my words.”

p.src: When tea had been served, Sun Quan said, “I have often heard Lu Zijing speak of your abilities. Now that I am fortunate enough to meet you, I venture to ask for your instruction.” Kongming replied, “I am a man of little talent and no learning, unworthy of so discerning an inquiry.” Sun Quan said, “You were recently at Xinye, assisting Governor Liu in battle against Cao Cao. You must know the true strength and weakness of his army.” Kongming replied, “Governor Liu had few soldiers and generals, while Xinye was a small city without provisions. How could he possibly hold out against Cao Cao?” Sun Quan asked, “How many troops does Cao Cao have in all?” Kongming replied, “His cavalry, infantry, and naval forces number somewhat over a million.” Sun Quan asked, “Surely that figure is false?” Kongming replied, “It is no falsehood. Cao Cao already had two hundred thousand Qingzhou troops when he occupied Yanzhou; after defeating Yuan Shao, he gained another five or six hundred thousand; he newly recruited three or four hundred thousand more in the Central Plains; and now he has acquired another two or three hundred thousand troops from Jingzhou. By that reckoning, his forces cannot number fewer than one and a half million. I said one million only because I feared alarming the gentlemen of the Southland.”

p.src: Hearing this from beside him, Lu Su turned pale and signaled to Kongming with his eyes, but Kongming pretended not to notice. Sun Quan asked, “How many battle-seasoned generals does Cao Cao have under his command?” Kongming replied, “His resourceful strategists and his generals practiced in warfare surely number more than one or two thousand!” Sun Quan asked, “Now that Cao Cao has pacified Jing and Chu, does he still harbor designs upon more distant lands?” Kongming replied, “At this very moment he is establishing camps along the river and preparing warships. If he does not intend to seize the Southland, what land can he be waiting to take?” Sun Quan said, “If he indeed intends to swallow up my lands, then whether to fight or not to fight—I ask you to decide the matter for me.” Kongming replied, “I have one piece of counsel, but I fear, General, that you will be unwilling to follow it.” Sun Quan said, “I should like to hear your lofty opinion.” Kongming said, “Formerly, when all within the realm was in chaos, you, General, rose in the Southland, while Governor Liu gathered followers south of the Han River, and both contended with Cao Cao for the empire. Now Cao Cao has cut down his greatest adversaries, and the land is for the most part pacified; recently he also conquered Jingzhou, and his might shakes all within the seas; even a hero has nowhere to employ his valor. That is why Governor Liu fled here. I pray you, General, measure your strength and act accordingly. If you can use the people of Wu and Yue to withstand the forces of the Central Plains, you had best break with Cao Cao at once; but if you cannot, why not follow the advice of your many counselors, still your troops, bind up your armor, and face north in submission to him?”

p.src: Before Sun Quan could answer, Kongming continued, “Outwardly, General, you profess submission, yet inwardly you harbor doubts and divided intentions. If you fail to decide when matters are urgent, disaster will be upon you in no time!” Sun Quan said, “If what you say is truly so, why has Governor Liu not surrendered to Cao Cao?” Kongming replied, “In former times Tian Heng was but a brave man of Qi, yet even he upheld righteousness and refused disgrace; how much more so Governor Liu, a scion of the imperial house, whose matchless gifts win the admiration of all worthy men? If his undertaking does not prosper, that is Heaven’s will. How could he ever abase himself beneath another?”

p.src: When Sun Quan heard these words from Kongming, his face suddenly flared with anger. He swept his robes aside, rose, and withdrew into the rear hall. The others all dispersed with derisive smiles. Lu Su reproached Kongming, saying, “Sir, why did you speak such words? It is fortunate that my lord is broad-minded and magnanimous and did not rebuke you to your face. Your words showed far too much contempt for my lord.” Kongming threw back his head and laughed. “How can he be so incapable of tolerating others? I have a plan of my own for defeating Cao Cao, but since he did not ask me, I deliberately said nothing.” Lu Su said, “If you truly have a sound plan, I shall ask my lord to seek your instruction.” Kongming said, “I regard Cao Cao’s million-strong host as no more than a swarm of ants! One sweep of my hand, and they will all be ground to pulp!”

p.src: Upon hearing this, Lu Su went into the rear hall to see Sun Quan. Sun Quan’s anger had not yet subsided. Turning to Lu Su, he said, “Kongming has insulted me beyond endurance!” Lu Su said, “I also reproached Kongming for it, but he laughed instead and said that my lord could not tolerate others, and that he would not lightly disclose his plan for defeating Cao Cao. Why does my lord not ask him for it?” Sun Quan’s anger turned to delight. “So Kongming has an excellent plan and deliberately provoked me with his words. In a moment of shallow judgment, I nearly ruined a great undertaking.” He promptly returned to the hall with Lu Su and invited Kongming to resume their conversation. On seeing Kongming, Sun Quan apologized: “I offended your dignity just now. I trust you will not hold it against me.” Kongming also apologized: “My words were offensive. I beg your forgiveness.” Sun Quan invited Kongming into the rear hall and entertained him with wine.

p.src: After several rounds of wine, Sun Quan said, “Throughout his life Cao Cao has hated Lü Bu, Liu Biao, Yuan Shao, Yuan Shu, Governor Liu, and myself. Now the other heroes have all perished, and only Governor Liu and I remain. I cannot surrender the whole land of Wu to another’s control. My decision is made. None but Governor Liu can join me in resisting Cao Cao. Yet after his recent defeat, how can Governor Liu withstand this peril?” Kongming replied, “Though Governor Liu has suffered a recent defeat, Guan Yunchang still commands ten thousand elite troops; and the fighting men of Jiangxia under Liu Qi also number no fewer than ten thousand. Cao Cao’s host is weary from its long march. In its recent pursuit of Governor Liu, the light cavalry covered three hundred li in a single day and night. This is what is meant by the saying, ‘At the end of its flight, even the bolt of a mighty crossbow cannot pierce the flimsy silk of Lu.’ Moreover, men of the north are unaccustomed to naval warfare. The soldiers and people of Jingzhou who submitted to Cao Cao did so only under compulsion, not from their true desire. If you, General, can truly join strength and purpose with Governor Liu, Cao Cao’s army will certainly be defeated. Once defeated, Cao Cao’s army will surely retreat north. Then the power of Jingzhou and Wu will grow, and the threefold balance of the realm will take shape. The decisive moment for success or failure is today. The decision rests with you alone, General.”

p.src: When Zhang Zhao learned that Sun Quan intended to raise an army, he consulted with the others and said, “We have fallen into Kongming’s trap!” He hurried in to see Sun Quan and said, “We have heard that my lord intends to raise an army and contend with Cao Cao. My lord, consider for yourself: how do you compare with Yuan Shao? In former days, when Cao Cao had few troops and scant commanders, he was still able to defeat Yuan Shao in a single campaign. How much less can he be taken lightly today, when he marches south at the head of a million men? If you heed Zhuge Liang’s words and recklessly set the troops in motion, it will be what is called carrying firewood to put out a fire.” Sun Quan merely bowed his head and said nothing. Gu Yong said, “Because Liu Bei was defeated by Cao Cao, he now wishes to borrow the forces of our land east of the Yangtze to resist him. Why should my lord allow himself to be used by Liu Bei? I beg you to heed Zibu’s counsel.”

After Zhang Zhao and the others had gone out, Lu Su entered and said, “Just now Zhang Zibu and the others again urged my lord not to mobilize the army and strongly advocated surrender. They are all ministers concerned with preserving their own lives and protecting their wives and children; their counsel is intended only for their own benefit. I beg my lord not to listen to them.” Sun Quan remained deep in thought. Lu Su said, “If my lord continues to hesitate, you will surely be led astray by the others.” Sun Quan said, “Withdraw for the moment and allow me to consider the matter thoroughly.” Lu Su then withdrew. At that time, some of the military officers wished to fight, while all the civil officials wished to surrender; opinions flew back and forth without agreement.

p.src: Now Sun Quan withdrew to his inner residence, where he could neither sleep nor eat in peace, wavering and unable to decide. If I choose to fight, I fear our few cannot withstand his many; yet if I choose to surrender, I also fear that Cao Cao will not spare me. For this reason, I waver and cannot decide.” Lady Wu said, “Why do you not remember the words my elder sister spoke on her deathbed?” Sun Quan was like a drunkard suddenly sobered, or a dreamer newly awakened, and recalled those words.
